dd.outlook: Two cases (next three years, a year)
dd.f.quality_of_earnings: Adjusted EBITDA {amount}, {signed} against reported, after owner costs and one-offs. Re-price on this number.
dd.f.inventory_write_down: Inventory is overstated by {pct}. About {amount} must be written off, and net assets fall by as much.
dd.f.working_capital.good: Net working capital {amount} ({days} days of sales), lighter than the industry. Cash generation after closing is dependable.
dd.f.working_capital.neutral: Net working capital {amount} ({days} days of sales), in line with the industry. A fair peg for the deal.
dd.f.working_capital.bad: Net working capital {amount} ({days} days of sales), heavier than the industry. Growth ties up cash; set the peg high.
dd.f.net_debt: Net debt {amount}. Take it off the enterprise value to get what the seller receives for the shares.
dd.f.market_growth.good: The market grows {signed} a year: a tailwind.
dd.f.market_growth.neutral: The market grows {signed} a year: unremarkable. Growth has to come from the company.
dd.f.market_growth.bad: The market shrinks {signed} a year. Keep the growth case conservative.
dd.f.growth_vs_market.good: The company grows {pct} a year faster than its market: it is taking share.
dd.f.growth_vs_market.neutral: The company grows with its market.
dd.f.growth_vs_market.bad: The company grows {pct} a year slower than its market: it is losing share.
dd.f.customer_concentration.risk: Losing that customer would take about {amount} of revenue. Check the contract term and renewal.
dd.f.pricing_power: A brand or a process of its own: customers stay when prices rise. Plenty of room for a pricing review.
dd.f.contracted_revenue: Much of revenue is contracted or recurring, so the forecast is reliable.
dd.f.management.good: Management scores {score}/20. Fit to run the plan after closing.
dd.f.management.neutral: Management scores {score}/20. One or two key seats need strengthening.
dd.f.management.bad: Management scores {score}/20. Consider a management change in the 100-day plan.
dd.f.capex_backlog: About {amount} of deferred capex must be spent within a year or two of closing. Take it off the price or fund it.
dd.f.aging_equipment: Old equipment needs about {amount} a year in replacements, which comes out of free cash flow.
dd.f.single_plant: All production sits in one plant: one accident stops revenue. Check insurance and contingency plans.
dd.f.key_person: Heavy reliance on one person. If they leave, growth could fall {pct} a year for six months. A retention package is needed.
dd.f.environmental: Soil and effluent clean-up is estimated at about {amount}. Seek a seller indemnity, an escrow or a price cut.
dd.f.labor_dispute: {pct} unionized with a collective agreement up for renewal: a dispute is likely. Avoid headcount cuts.
dd.f.change_of_control: Key contracts carry change-of-control clauses: customer consent is needed before closing.
dd.f.permits: Regulatory permits are reviewed on a change of owner. Leave room in the closing timetable.
dd.f.clean_title: No material legal defect in the shares, the assets or the contracts.
